SPECIALIST FLAG SERVICE

When the flag
won’t move.

Describe a flag that will not raise or lower so the operating system and access needs can be assessed.

GET A QUOTE

START WITH THE RIGHT DETAILS

A stuck flag can involve the rope, clips, pulley or internal operating mechanism. The visible symptom helps define the first assessment; it does not establish the cause on its own.

01

What happens

Explain whether the line moves at all, whether the problem is intermittent, and whether anything changed before the issue began.

02

Where it stops

Describe the flag’s position from the ground and whether the rope appears tangled or caught. Photos can help without approaching the equipment.

03

Safe next step

Stop forcing the mechanism. Mention any loose components, unusual pole movement or restrictions around the display.

MAKE YOUR REQUEST USEFUL

A better brief.
A clearer quote.

Include approximate pole height, internal or external halyard, the current flag position and safe ground-level images. Access requirements are confirmed after review.

Service availability, equipment access and the final scope depend on the location and reported conditions.

REQUEST SERVICE

GOOD TO KNOW

A few useful answers.

Should I pull harder to free the flag?

No. Forcing a jammed system can worsen damage or create a falling-object hazard. Leave the mechanism alone and request an assessment.

What if I do not know the model or dimensions?

Send the information you have, including existing records and photos taken from a safe position. Do not climb, dismantle or alter the display to complete the enquiry.
